main.why: How real databases handle processes, memory and parallelism, which textbooks skip.

main.why: Eight years of priorities moving from write amplification to space to CPU.

main.title: The Part of PostgreSQL We Hate the Most
main.why: Postgres MVCC copies the whole row on each update, causing bloat and vacuum pain.

main.why: Living with it. Measure bloat, drop unused indexes and tune autovacuum.

main.title: An Overview of Query Optimization in Relational Systems
main.why: How plans are searched and costed, starting from System R.

main.why: Row count estimates are often far off, and matter more than the cost model.

main.why: Snapshot isolation. SQL's isolation levels are vague, and snapshot isolation still allows write skew.

main.title: Serializable Isolation for Snapshot Databases
main.why: Detects write skew so snapshot isolation becomes serializable, as PostgreSQL does.

A proxy tier that cuts connections to Meta's ZippyDB hosts by 97%.
Replacing a dead primary with a replica in 10 to 13 seconds.
Splitting one Postgres into 480 shards, migrated with double writes.

main.title: C-Store: A Column-oriented DBMS
main.why: Stores data by column, so a query reads only the columns it needs.

main.title: MonetDB/X100: Hyper-Pipelining Query Execution
main.why: Vectorized execution. Operators process a batch of values per call instead of one row.

main.title: DuckDB: an Embeddable Analytical Database
main.why: An in-process database like SQLite, but columnar and built for analytics.

main.title: What Goes Around Comes Around... And Around...
main.why: Twenty years of SQL replacements, and how SQL absorbed their best ideas.
